title: Measure 40 Worm Feeding with Bioluminescent Bacteria After Drug Treatment
author: Serena Ding
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.53ng8me
materials: Initialise the IVIS system via the LivingImage software.

Set up imaging parameters within the LivingImage software interface. Set stage temperature to 20 °C , designate auto-saving directory for acquired images, and set up acquisition sequence parameters. Bioluminescence acquisition parameters: subject height: 0.5 cm; field of view: C; expososure: 1 second; frame interval: 6 minutes; excitation: block; emission: open; luminescence binning: 4; photograph binning: 4; luminescence F/stop: 1; photograph F/stop: 1; batch sequence: true; sequence 1 length: 99; sequence 2 length: 35. These imaging parameters have been determined in advance for the experiment and are saved as a .xsq configuration file, which can be loaded into the imaging software.

steps.title: Prepare Bioluminescent Bacteria Stock
steps.instruction: Streak out bioluminescent bacteria frozen stock onto an LB plate containing 50 μg/mL ampicillin and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: Note: A streaked plate can be re-used within 1 month if single colonies are available; otherwise, re-streak onto a new LB/ampicillin plate.

steps.title: Bleach Synchronize Animals
steps.instruction: Bleach synchronize animals from three 60mm plates containing plenty of gravid hermaphrodites.

substeps.instruction: Leave on rotator at 20 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare Drug Plates
steps.instruction: Make up serotonin and naloxone drug plates and store them in the dark at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Culture Bioluminescent Bacteria
steps.instruction: At approximately 5pm on Day -1, prepare a bacterial culture in a 300 mL volumetric flask.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 mL LB broth and 100 μL ampicillin stock solution (50mg/mL).
Inoculate with a single colony of bioluminescent bacteria from the streaked plate.
Incubate at 37 °C shaking at 220 rpm overnight.

steps.title: Prepare Bacteria for Seeding
steps.instruction: At approximately 10am on Day 0, remove the overnight culture from the shaking incubator and leave at room temperature on the bench until use.

substeps.instruction: Do not store at 4 °C as this abolishes the signal.
Swirl the flask to resuspend bacteria cells that may have settled.

steps.title: Seed Imaging Plates
steps.instruction: Seed the bioluminescent bacteria onto 35 mm imaging plates.

substeps.instruction: Seed 20 μL of the bacteria culture onto the center of each plate.
Dry the plates in a laminar flow hood (setting II) for 30 minutes.
Retrieve plates from the hood and label with sample names.

steps.title: Starve Worms
steps.instruction: Transfer worms to an unseeded NGM plate to starve for 1 hour.

substeps.instruction: Use a glass pipette with a medicine dropper bulb for transfer.

steps.title: Drug Treatment
steps.instruction: Expose the starved worms to drugs for 1 hour at 20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Harvest starved worms using M9 into a 15 mL tube.
Pellet worms by spinning at 1500 rpm/210 rcf (ascending 9, descending 7) and aspire the supernatant, leaving the loose pellet intact.

steps.title: Prepare Worms for Imaging
steps.instruction: Harvest synchronized adult worms and remove remaining bacteria.

substeps.instruction: Harvest worms using 2 mL of M9 buffer and transfer to a 15 mL tube.
Wash twice with M9 buffer by topping up the tube, spinning at 1500 rpm/210 rcf (ascending 9, descending 7), and aspiring the supernatant.
Leave the loose worm pellet after the final wash.

steps.title: Transfer Worms to Imaging Plates
steps.instruction: Transfer exactly 40 starved worms to each imaging plate using a glass pipette with a medicine dropper bulb and a manual click counter.

substeps.instruction: Keep the droplet small to ensure absorption into the media within a couple of minutes.
Use a P20 pipette with a few microliters of M9 to carefully remove excess worms if necessary, then re-count.
Place the lid back onto the imaging plate.

steps.title: Perform IVIS Imaging
steps.instruction: Image the samples using the IVIS imaging system.

substeps.instruction: Warm drug plates (prepared the previous day) at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Place samples inside a cardboard box, then a styrofoam box, and transport carefully to the IVIS system.
Place samples inside the IVIS chamber within the laser grid guidelines and close the door.
Vortex imaging samples for 10s on the lowest setting to disperse aggregates and randomize worm positions.
Start acquisition via software exactly 1 min after the vortex start.

steps.title: Analyze Imaging Data
steps.instruction: Process the acquired image sequence using LivingImage software.

substeps.instruction: Measure radiance (photons/s) for a defined region of interest across the acquisition sequence.
Export the signal as a tab-delimited text file for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Post-Imaging Maintenance
steps.instruction: Re-feed worms using a glass pipette and incubate at 20 °C, monitoring plates to ensure food availability.

steps.title: Record Bacterial Density
steps.instruction: Measure the bacteria culture optical density with a spectrophotometer for the record.
